title: Graph of y = sin⁻¹x
back: Rises from $(-1,-\frac\pi2)$ through the origin to $(1,\frac\pi2)$. Domain $[-1,1]$, range $[-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2]$: the sine curve reflected in $y=x$.

title: Principal branch of sin⁻¹x
back: Same interval for $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}x$ (without 0) and, with open ends, for $\tan^{-1}x$.

title: Principal branch of cos⁻¹x
back: Same interval for $\sec^{-1}x$ (without $\frac\pi2$) and, with open ends, for $\cot^{-1}x$.

title: sin⁻¹ of a negative number
back: The minus comes out. Also true for $\tan^{-1}$ and $\operatorname{cosec}^{-1}$.

title: cos⁻¹ of a negative number
back: The minus becomes $\pi-$. Also true for $\cot^{-1}$ and $\sec^{-1}$. So $\cos^{-1}(-\frac12)=\pi-\frac\pi3=\frac{2\pi}{3}$.

title: When does sin⁻¹(sin θ) = θ?
back: Otherwise bring the angle into the branch first: $\sin^{-1}(\sin\frac{2\pi}{3})=\sin^{-1}(\sin\frac\pi3)=\frac\pi3$.

title: Domain of sin⁻¹(ax + b)
back: Solve the double inequality for $x$. Example: $\sin^{-1}(2x-1)$ needs $0\le x\le1$.

title: Substitution for simplest form
back: And $\sqrt{x^2-a^2}$: $x=a\sec\theta$. After simplifying, go back to $x$ with $\theta=\sin^{-1}\frac xa$ and so on.
